**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (298 K, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (in H₂) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm) |
| | Dielectric constant | ~1.3 (at 1 MHz) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (H₂(g)) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy (H₂(g)) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HX → H⁺ + X⁻) in aqueous solution; forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (ΔH° = –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Redox potential (H⁺/H₂) | 0 V (standard hydrogen electrode) |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (≈0.0006 M) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Variable; e.g., ~0.5 g L⁻¹ in ethanol |
| | Flame color | Blue (non-luminous) |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 1.6 × 10⁻⁵ % natural abundance |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion and radiolabeling |
| **Applications & Roles** | Fuel cell chemistry | H₂ + O₂ → H₂O (electrochemical) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid H₂ + liquid O₂ |
| | Metallurgy | Reducing agent for metal oxides |
| | Chemical synthesis | Hydride donor (NaH, LiAlH₄) |
| | Astrophysics | Primary fuel in stellar nucleosynthesis (pp‑chain, CNO cycle) |
| | Fusion research | Deuterium–tritium fusion (D + T → He + n) |
| | Environmental science | Indicator of water quality (H₂S, NH₃) |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability range (air) | 4 % – 75 % (v/v) |
| | Explosion limit | 4 % (lower) / 75 % (upper) |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic; high pressure can cause asphyxiation |
| | Storage | Cryogenic tanks (–253 °C) or high‑pressure cylinders (up to 700 bar) |
| | Detection | Hydrogen sensors (metal‑oxide, catalytic combustion) |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, with one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms covalent bonds readily; reacts with oxygen, halogens, and many metals.
- **Energy carrier**: Used in fuel cells and rocket propulsion; potential clean energy source.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium, deuterium, and tritium each have distinct physical and nuclear properties.
- **Spectroscopic importance**: Hydrogen’s spectral lines (Lyman, Balmer) are fundamental in astronomy and plasma diagnostics.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
